Title: Add Color Swatch
Content: Objective Add color swatches to custom palette. Location Property Editor Material Color Color Palette Window Add Operation Select a desired object Avatar/Fabric/Button/Topstitch/Etc. Click on Color in the Property Editor. The Color Palette window appears. Select a desired color from Open Palette or Palette Library. Follow the indicated guideline below: Color Palette Window Add The selected color is now being added to the custom palette.

Title: Palette Library
Content: Objective Load or delete a palette file in the Library window. Location Property Editor Material Color Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Material Color Color Palette window appears. Click on + button on the top-right of the window. Open File window appears. Select a desired palette file (*.aco/*.aso) to load. The selected file is now being added to the Palette Library. Note: Change Display Click on Display icon at the bottom-right corner of the Palette Library to change the display for the color swatches. Copy to Custom Palette Select a palette to be copied, then click on Copy to Custom Palette icon at the bottom-right corner of the window. Search Color (ver. 11) Search a similar color with the name of the color or the selected color.

Title: Color Palette
Content: Import existing color palettes from llustrator, Photoshop, or customize an own color palette and utilize it for design works (ver2.2.0).

Title: Eyedropper
Content: Objective Use Eyedropper tool to extract any desired colors not only from Marvelous Designer, but any other websites or images just by clicking the colors. Location Property Editor Material Color Eyedropper Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Material Color Eyedropper Move mouse cursor to desired area. The mouse cursor icon is now being changed to an eyedropper-shaped. Click on a desired area to extract a color. The extracted color sample appears in the window. To exit the tool, click on the Eyedropper icon again or press ESC on keyboard.

Title: Delete Texture
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary texture images as needed. Location Main Menu Materials Texture Edit Texture 2D Toolbar Edit Texture Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Texture Edit Texture 2D Toolbar Edit Texture Right-click on the texture to delete. Click Delete Texture from the pop-up menu. The selected texture image is now being deleted.

Title: Edit Texture
Content: Objective Modify the Fabric's grainline and location for individual Patterns, and texture image's rotation and size for individual Fabric. Location Main Menu Materials Texture Edit Texture 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Texture Operation Move Follow the indicated location above. Click Drag texture image applied to Pattern with the left mouse button. The selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being moved. Zoom In/Out Follow the indicated location above. Select a Pattern to zoom in/out. A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. Click Drag the diagonal line. Enlarge or reduce the size of the selected texture image. The selected texture image is now being adjustable while maintaining its horizontal and vertical ratios. Click Drag the horizontal line in order to enlarge/reduce the texture image to up/down and left/right. All texture images applied to the same Fabric are now being adjustable corresponding to the axis direction. Alternatively, select a Fabric and enter the image's Width and Height value in Property Editor Material Texture Transformation. The width and height of all texture images applied to the same Fabric are now being adjusted. Rotate Follow the indicated location above. Select a Pattern to rotate the Fabric. A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. A circle appears when mouse-over the curve. Drag around the circumference of the circle. The selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being rotated. Rotate Grainline Follow the indicated location above. Click on a Pattern to rotate its grainline. The selected Pattern's grainline is now being in black color. Drag around the activated grainline, when the mouse cursor becomes in a shape of circular rotation. The selected grainline is now being rotated and so as the texture image. Alternatively, select a Fabric and enter the angle value for grainline in Property Editor Fabric Grain Direction. The selected grainline is now being rotated and so as the texture image. Simulate once it is adjusted. The draping is now being adjusted according to the change in grainline. Align Grain Parallel to Selected Follow the indicated location above. Select a Pattern to rotate its grain. The grain of the selected Pattern is activated. When multiple Patterns are selected, only the last Pattern's grain is activated, but the configuration is applied to all Patterns. Right click on the Pattern and select Align Grain Parallel to Selected. All selectable segments are highlighted. Hover the mouse over the segment which the grain is to be aligned with. The segment is highlighted in light blue. The grain rotates. When the selected segment is a curve, the grain rotates based on a line connecting the ends of the curve. Click the desired segment. The grain rotates parallel to the selected line. When multiple Patterns are selected, all their grains rotate accordingly. Note: After selecting a Fabric, navigate to Property Editor Material Transformation Texture to type in the texture's width, height, and angle. Right-click to input the exact values while rotating textures and grainlines. Edit back of texture when you change Garment Rendering Style as Back Texture Surface (ver. MD10)

Title: Edit Texture (v.2.2.0)
Content: Objective Use this function to edit the size, rotation, location on Pattern, etc of textures applied to Fabrics. Location Main Menu Materials Texture Edit Texture (2D) / Edit Texture (3D) Toolbar Edit Texture (2D) / Edit Texture (3D) Operation Move Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Texture Edit Texture (2D) / Edit Texture (3D) Toolbar Edit Texture (2D) / Edit Texture (3D) Click Drag texture image applied to Pattern with the left mouse button. The selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being moved. Zoom In/Out Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Texture Edit Texture (2D) / Edit Texture (3D) Toolbar Edit Texture (2D) / Edit Texture (3D) Click Drag the red diagonal point on the yellow circle. Zoom in or out the texture. All texture images applied to the same Fabric are now being adjustable while maintaining its horizontal and vertical ratios. Click Drag the red point at the end of cross hair in order to enlarge/reduce the texture horizontally or vertically. All texture images applied to the same Fabric are now being adjustable corresponding to the axis direction. Alternatively, select a fabric and enter the image's width and height value (mm) in Property Editor Material Texture Transformation. The Width and Height of all texture images applied to the same Fabric are now being adjusted. Note: If Lock Aspect Ratio is being checked, the horizontal and vertical ratios maintain. Rotate Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Texture Edit Texture (2D) / Edit Texture (3D) Toolbar Edit Texture (2D) / Edit Texture (3D) Grab the yellow circle and drag around its circumference. Only the selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being rotated. Alternatively, select a fabric and enter the Angle value in Property Editor Material Texture Transformation. The angle of all texture images applied to the same Fabric are now being rotated.

Title: Desaturation
Content: Objective Use this function to maintain the texture of texture images or patterns while changing colors. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Material Texture Desaturation Operation Shadow Intensity Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Material Texture Desaturation Enter the Shadow Intensity value directly or move the scrollbar to adjust. The Shadow Intensity is now being adjusted and applied. Shadow Brightness Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Material Texture Desaturation Enter the Shadow Brightness value directly or move the scrollbar to adjust. The Shadow Brightness is now being adjusted and applied.

Title: Fabric Texture Normal Map
Content: Objective Apply Normal Maps to express bumpy surfaces such as twill, corduroy, and leather. Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Fabric Item Property Editor Material Normal Map Operation Fabric Normal Map Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Tab Fabric Item Property Editor Material Normal Map An intensity value range of -10 to 10 can be adjusted with the scrollbar or entered directly. Depending on the normal map applied, the visual depth will change as you scroll from negative to positive values. Apply Fabric Normal Map Image Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Tab Fabric Item Property Editor Material Normal Map Click on Open button. Select and load the desired texture image file. The selected image is now applied. Note : Although a Normal Map is automatically generated for Fabric textures, it is recommended to use third party solutions to generate more distinctive normal map effects. This feature can also be used to overlay a different texture above the existing texture. The normal map image size can also be adjusted via: Fabric Property Editor Material Texture Transformation. Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to the Open icon next to the Normal Map menu in the Property Editor (ver4.0.0). Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to an object in the program, then select the correct map: texture, normal, specular (ver4.0.0).

Title: Rename Fabric
Content: Objective Rename Fabrics to distinguish one from another. Location Object Browser Select Fabric Property Editor Edit Name Object Browser Select Fabric Property Editor Click Name Field Object Browser Fabric Tab Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (On Fabric) Rename Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Select Fabric Property Editor Edit Name Object Browser Select Fabric Property Editor Double Click Name Field Object Browser Fabric Tab Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (On Fabric) Rename The selected fabric's name is now being changed and applied.

Title: Add Fabric Information
Content: Objective Add Fabric information in the Property Editor. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Set a Fabric's properties in the Property Editor. Once the setting is done, click Save button at the top-right corner of the Property Editor to complete. Note: Type and Content fields have been added to the Property Editor. Enter the respective information in these fields (ver3.1.0).

Title: Preview Fabric Information
Content: Objective Preview Fabric information in the Library window. Location Library Fabric Fabric File (.zfab) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Library Fabric Fabric File (.zfab) Preview of Fabric files is now being displayed below the Library section. Note: Only fabric files saved in Marvelous Designer 4 and above are allowed to display Fabric information preview. For any fabric files created in previous versions, need to be saved again in ver3.1.0 or above (ver3.1.0).

Title: Vizoo File Compatibility
Content: Objective Marvelous Designer is compatible with Vizoo 3D which scans actual material information (Color/Specular/Normal Map). Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Tab Right-click on a Fabric style. Select Import xTex File from the menu and load the relevant xTex file.

Title: Delete Fabric
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary Fabric styles from the Fabric list. Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Delete Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Tab Delete The selected Fabric style is now being deleted from the Fabric list. Note: It can also be deleted by selecting a Fabric and pressing Delete key on keyboard. Fabrics can only be deleted when it is not being applied to any of Patterns.

Title: Copy Fabric
Content: Objective Copy and modify an existing Fabric in order to change Fabric properties partially. Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Copy Operation Object Browser Select a fabric style to copy in the Fabric tab. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Tab Copy A new Fabric item with the same properties of the selected Fabric item is now being created.

Title: Show UV Guide
Content: Objective Check UV guide in the 2D window. Location Main Menu Display 2D Pattern Show UV Guide 2D Toolbar Show_UV_Guide.png Show UV Guide Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu Display 2D Pattern Show UV Guide 2D Toolbar Show_UV_Guide.png Show UV Guide A marquee box appears encompassing all Patterns in the 2D window. Note: Modify the UV guide by using the image2015-8-17_14_19_14.png Edit UV tool.

Title: Remeshing to Retopology (Selected)  (ver. 5.1.4)
Content: Objective Remesh selected pattern and generate retopology lines along the remeshed polygon. Location Right-click pattern pop-up menu (3D window) Remeshing to Retopology Operation Click the menu specified in Location. A polygon count input dialog will pop up. Enter the desired number of polygons and click the Apply button. The mesh of the selected patterns is rearranged into an aligned quad mesh. Retopology lines are generated along the remeshed polygons. To return to the previous status, right-click on the pattern and select 'Undo Remeshing' from the pop-up menu.

Title: Show Mesh
Content: Objective Show or hide the mesh structure that 3D Garments are composed of. Mesh forms may vary depending on Patterns, Internal Lines, and Sewing state. Location 2D Pattern Window Main Menu Display 2D Pattern Rendering Style Mesh 3D Garment Window Main Menu Display 3D Garment Rendering Style Mesh 3D Icon Garment Rendering Style Mesh

Title: Deactivate (Pattern Only)/Activate
Content: Objective Deactivated Patterns are considered nonexistent in the 3D window. Therefore the rest of the Patterns simulate through the deactivated Patterns. The general use of the function is to prevent complicated details, such as pleats or slits, from collapsing. When deactivating specific Patterns, the Simulation speed gets faster as it excludes them from the calculation. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern Only) / Activate 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern Only) / Activate Operation Follow the indicated guideline: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern Only) / Activate 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern Only) / Activate The selected Pattern is now being deactivated/activated. Note: 3D Statement

Title: Deactivate(Pattern & Sewing)/Activate
Content: Objective Deactivated Patterns are considered as nonexistence in the 3D window. Therefore the rest of the Patterns simulate through the deactivated Patterns. The function is generally used to keep complicated details such as pleats or slits, from avoiding collapsing (ver2.3.0). Note: When deactivating certain Patterns, the Simulation speed gets faster as it excludes them from calculation. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern &amp Sewing) / Activate 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern &amp Sewing) / Activate Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern &amp Sewing) / Activate 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern &amp Sewing) / Activate The selected Patterns and connected Sewing Lines are now being deactivated/activated. Note: 3D Statement

Title: Reverse Arrangement Horizontally/Vertically
Content: Objective Flip 3D Garment Patterns horizontally and vertically while maintaining its curvature. Note: Flipping Patterns while maintaining its curvature is only applicable for patterns arranged with Arrangement Points. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Reverse-Arrange Horizontally / Vertically Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Reverse-Arrange Horizontally / Vertically The selected Pattern is now being flipped over horizontally/vertically while maintaining its curvature.

Title: Flip Horizontally/Vertically
Content: Objective Flip a Pattern horizontally or vertically in the 3D window. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Flip Horizontally / Flip Vertically Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Flip Horizontally / Flip Vertically The selected Pattern is now being rotated 180 on the Y axis (vertically) or X axis (horizontally).

Title: Smart Arrangement
Content: Objective Arrange a new Pattern onto an existing Pattern while maintaining 3D draping state (ver3.0.0). Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Smart Arrangement Operation Utilizing the sewing tools, sew a new Pattern to an existing Pattern that is being draped. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Smart Arrangement The selected Pattern is now being arranged to where it is sewn as draped.

Title: Superimpose
Content: Objective Arrange a newly sewn Pattern onto its corresponding Pattern. This function is helpful when arranging facings, linings, cuffs, collars and other pieces where they need to be arranged directly laying on another. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Superimpose (Over) / Superimpose (Under) / Superimpose (Side) Operation Using the sewing tools, sew a new Pattern to an existing Pattern that is being draped. Follow the indicated guidelines below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Superimpose (Over) / Superimpose (Under) / Superimpose (Side) The selected Pattern is now being arranged accordingly. Note: This function only applies to Patterns that are already being sewn together.

Title: Reset 2D Arrangement
Content: Objective Spread and arrange the entire or the selected patterns in the 3D window identical to 2D window state. Location Selected Pattern 3D Toolbar Select/Move right-click menu on a 3D pattern Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected) All Pattern Main Menu 3D Garment Reset 2D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar Reset 2D Arrangement (All) Operation Selected Pattern Select a 3D Pattern to reset its arrangement identical to 2D window state. Note: Press Shift key on keyboard to select multiple Patterns. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move right-click menu on a 3D pattern Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected) The selected Pattern is now being rearranged to match 2D window state. All Pattern Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Reset 2D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar Reset 2D Arrangement (All) The entire Pattern is now being rearranged to match 2D window state.

Title: Direct Positioning
Content: Objective Activate Direct Positioning to click to easily arrange Patterns and OBJs. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Click 3D Pattern or OBJ Direct Positioning Operation Follow the path: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Click 3D Pattern or OBJ Direct Positioning Hover the mouse over a Garment or Avatar. The selected Pattern or OBJ moves along with the mouse cursor. Click to place the Pattern in the desired location. Note: When arranging Patterns, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to restrict Pattern rotation (ver4.0.0).

Title: Move with Arrow Keys (3D)
Content: Objective Select Patterns in the 3D window, then use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move them in specific increments. Location Move Patterns with Arrow Keys Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Set Specific Movement Increment Main Menu Preferences Grid Properties Property Editor 3D Arrow Key Movement Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) Grid Properties Property Editor 3D Arrow Key Movement Operation Move Patterns with Arrow Keys Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select Patterns or trims in the 3D window. Selected Patterns or trims are highlighted in yellow. Use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move the selected Pattern or trim. Arrow Keys Description Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive y-axis. The Garment moves upwards. Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative y-axis. The Garment moves downwards. Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative x-axis. The Garment moves to the left. Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive x-axis. The Garment moves to the right. + Ctrl Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative z-axis. The Garment moves away from you. + Ctrl Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive z-axis. The Garment moves towards you. Set Specific Movement Increment Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Preferences Grid Properties Property Editor 3D Arrow Key Movement Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) Grid Properties Property Editor 3D Arrow Key Movement Enter the desired distance moved with each arrow key input.

Title: Arrangement Property Setting
Content: Objective Set arrangement property details after arranging patterns with Arrangement Points. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select 3D Pattern Property Editor Arrangement Note: The arrangement properties are only accessible for Patterns that are arranged by Arrangement Points. Operation Arrange Patterns with Arrangement Points Follow the guidelines below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select 3D Pattern Property Editor Arrangement Point Name Shows which arrangement point the selected pattern is on top of. Shape Style Changes the arrangement bounding volume pattern to be flat or curved. Position X Moves horizontally according to the arrangement bounding volume. Position Y Moves vertically according to the arrangement bounding volume. Offset Adjusts the offset and curvature between the arrangement bounding volume and the pattern. Orientation Changes the pattern's direction according to the arrangement bounding volume.

Title: Open/Save Bounding Volume
Content: Objective Save newly created Bounding Volume, open and use previously saved Arrangement Points. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Open / Save Operation Open Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Open Open File window appears. Select desired file and click Open to load. Save Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Save Save File window appears. Select desired location to store. Enter desired file name and click Save. A .pan file is now being created.

Title: Delete Bounding Voulme
Content: Objective Delete Bounding Volume no longer in need. Note: When deleting Bounding Volume, be aware that all corresponding Arrangement Points also get deleted from the 3D window. Select the Arrangement Points and assign them to another Bounding Volume to avoid any loss. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Delete Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Delete Selected Bounding Volume is now being deleted from the Bounding Volume list and the 3D window. Note: Selecting a Bounding Volume in the 3D window and pressing Delete key on keyboard also allows to delete it.
